question: Can I stake my XLM for passive income, and are there plans for native staking?

golden.answer: Stellar does not use proof-of-stake, so holding XLM does not natively stake it or earn protocol staking rewards. If a third party advertises 'XLM staking,' it is offering its own product, not activating a native network feature; investigate its custody, lockup, withdrawal, counterparty, and scam risks independently. Never send a secret key or funds to a promoter just to 'activate' staking. As of 2026-11-02, a live sweep of the official accepted and proposed CAP repository shows no native-staking or validator-reward CAP. That is a dated record claim, not a promise that future governance can never change. In October 2026, SDF published a discussion paper on a possible fee-pool-funded reward for XLM locked for a fixed term; SDF says it has not decided to fund or support any such mechanism, and that locked XLM would not secure the network or confer validator rights.
keyFacts: States that Stellar has no native proof-of-stake reward for holding XLM.
Treats a third-party yield product as different from native staking.
avoid: Do NOT say SDF runs an official staking program.
Do NOT call every third-party yield product native staking.
Do NOT say native staking will never exist or present an undated absence-of-plans claim.
Do NOT say SDF's October 2026 fee-pool rewards paper was adopted or is proof-of-stake staking.
golden.notes: Negative/status claim requires blind re-derivation before landing. SDF's October 2026 fee-pool rewards discussion paper (stellar.org/xlm-utility) is an undecided proposal for community feedback; an accurate dated mention of it is correct and does not contradict the CAP-sweep negative.
